item.title: Amidst cold wave J&K, Ladakh likely to face 34% power deficit
item.description: NAVVNEET DUBEY Jammu: With the advent of Chillai-Kalan -Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh is likely to witness a power deficit of more than 34 percent in the coming fortnight. The officials said that in the anticipated power supply position in the northern region for December, Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh is likely to have a power shortage of 34.2 percent. item.title: Search operation underway after terrorists take food from house
item.description: Jammu: Security forces launched a search operation at a village in Jammu and Kashmir’s Udhampur district after terrorists reportedly took food from a house before escaping into the nearby forest area, officials said on Sunday. The joint search operation by police and paramilitary forces was underway at Chore Motu and its adjoining forest villages in the Majalta area, some 5 km west of the site of an earlier encounter that left a policeman dead, the officials said. item.title: J&K carries out pulse polio drive, CM Abdullah vows to make UT polio-free
item.description: Jammu: Jammu and Kashmir government on Sunday conducted a pulse polio drive across the Union territory, with Chief Minister Omar Abdullah urging parents to ensure that every child aged 0-5 years receives polio drops. Abdullah also reaffirmed the government’s commitment to making the UT a polio-free region. item.title: First foodgrain freight train reaches Kashmir; ‘Memorable occasion’, says LG
item.description: Srinagar: The first-ever foodgrain freight train of the Food Corporation of India (FCI) reached the Anantnag Goods Terminal here in Kashmir on Sunday, formally integrating the region with the national freight rail network, official said. “The freight rake, carrying approximately 1,384 tonnes of food grains loaded in wagons, was dispatched from Ajitwal Railway Station and successfully arrived at Anantnag Goods Terminal,” an official spokesman said. item.title: Snow, rain end dry spell in Kashmir; Srinagar records warmest winter night, key roads shut
item.description: Jammu: Snowfall in the higher reaches and rain across the plains marked the beginning of Chillai-Kalan — Kashmir’s 40-day harshest winter period — on Sunday, bringing much-needed relief from a prolonged dry spell, even as minimum temperatures rose sharply across the Valley. Srinagar recorded its warmest night of the winter season, with the mercury settling at 4 degrees Celsius — six notches above the seasonal average. item.title: Terrorism, drug mafia will always remain under our gun sight: J&K Police Chief
item.description: JAMMU: Jammu and Kashmir Police Chief Nalin Prabhat on Monday said that militancy and all other forms of crime will always remain under the strict vigil of the police force. Addressing a gathering in Kathua, DGP Prabhat said that whether it is drugs, gangsters, mafia or any other kind of crime, especially militancy, everything will remain in the sight of their guns. item.title: 2 J&K men arrested in Arunachal Pradesh for allegedly Spying for Pakistan
item.description: Itanagar, Dec 23: Arunachal Pradesh’s Itanagar police have arrested two more persons from Jammu and Kashmir’s Kupwara district for allegedly spying and collecting sensitive information for handlers based in Pakistan, officials said. The arrested persons have been identified as Aijaz Ahmed Bhat and Bashir Ahmad Ganai. With the latest arrests, the total number of accused held in the espionage case has risen to five.
